newsitem.title: USA: U.S. fund managers stay put on US debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fund managers stay put on US debt -- survey.

text.p: Money managers made no substantive changes on their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"For the third week running ... activity was again both limited and two-way," the report said.
"Money managers have been holding a duration exposure that is marginally short, and do not appear to be inclined to change at this point," it said.
In the week ended June 10, the cash/assets ratio fell to 8.63 percent from 9.09 percent on an arithmetic basis and declined to 6.00 percent from 6.18 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index slipped to 98.72 percent from 98.74 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 99.49 percent from 99.44 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.65 from 4.78 on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 4.50 from 4.38 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Nine percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 13 percent the week ending June 3.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
